topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
title: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus, Democratic Republic of the Congo
date_evidence:
Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus - Democratic Republic of the Congo

28 August 2026

See all DONs related to this event
key_claim: As of 26 August 2026 the Democratic Republic of the Congo had reported 5794 confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease cases and 2786 deaths at a crude case fatality ratio of 48.1%, across 60 health zones in six provinces, up from 54 health zones two weeks earlier.
frame_summary: WHO argues the epidemic is expanding faster than the response can detect and isolate cases, and that the binding weakness is late case recognition and unsafe care rather than any absence of a response plan.
verbatim_quote: As of 26 August 2026, a total of 5794 confirmed cases, including 2786 deaths, have been reported, corresponding to a crude case fatality ratio (CFR) of 48.1%.
verbatim_list: Cases have been reported from 60 health zones (HZ) across six provinces.
Delays in recognizing cases increase the likelihood of onward transmission within households, communities and healthcare facilities.
On 27 August, vaccination of health care workers using the Ervebo vaccine was initiated in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in some areas, including in Kisangani, Tshopo province.
Since 14 August 2026 when the last Disease Outbreak News was published, an additional 1129 confirmed cases, including 602 confirmed deaths, have been reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Although Ervebo is a safe vaccine, and effective against Ebola virus disease, it is not known whether it provides protection against the Bundibugyo virus in humans.
Thus, starting a clinical trial of the vaccine, alongside this wider use, is key to provide important new evidence and inform future use of the vaccine.

key_claim: The Director-General kept the PHEIC in place after the second Emergency Committee meeting on 18 August and issued a new section of temporary recommendations covering social measures, mass gatherings and domestic mobility, including road checkpoints and surveillance on inland waterways running to Kinshasa.
frame_summary: WHO argues the epidemic has outgrown clinical containment and now requires population-movement controls and timely payment of the response workforce, which places the burden on state capacity rather than on medical countermeasures.

verbatim_list: Postpone mass gatherings in areas with ongoing community BDV transmission.
health workforce management and protection, including timely payment of salaries and, as appropriate, hazard pay.

topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (Measles)
title: Measles Cases and Outbreaks
key_claim: As of 3 September 2026 the United States had recorded 3,134 confirmed measles cases in 47 jurisdictions with 38 new outbreaks, against 2,289 in all of 2025, while kindergarten MMR coverage has fallen to 92.4% from 95.2% in 2019 to 2020.
frame_summary: CDC attributes the recurrence and size of US outbreaks to kindergarten vaccination coverage having fallen below the level at which community immunity holds, framing this as a coverage problem rather than an importation problem.
verbatim_quote: At local levels, vaccine coverage rates may vary considerably, and pockets of unvaccinated people can exist in states with high vaccination coverage.
verbatim_list: As of September 3, 2026, 3,134 confirmed* measles cases were reported in the United States in 2026.

There have been 38 new outbreaks** reported in 2026, and 95% of confirmed cases (2,969 of 3,134) are outbreak-associated (1,594 from outbreaks starting in 2026 and 1,375 from outbreaks that started in 2025).

However, vaccination coverage among U.S. kindergartners has decreased from 95.2% during the 2019-2020 school year to 92.4% in the 2025-2026 school year, leaving approximately 280,000 kindergartners at risk during the 2025-2026 school year.
When more than 95% of people in a community are vaccinated (coverage >95%), most people are protected through community immunity (herd immunity).
Among these, 3,118 measles cases were reported by 47 jurisdictions

topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
title: Update on the review of measles elimination status
date_evidence:
Update on the review of measles elimination status

2 Mar 2026

Washington, D.C., 2 March 2026 (PAHO)
key_claim: PAHO will review the measles elimination status of the United States and Mexico in November 2026 at the annual meeting of the Regional Verification Commission, assessing re-establishment of endemic transmission over one year from outbreak onset, 20 January 2025 in the US.
frame_summary: PAHO frames the elimination verdict as a scheduled technical determination made on genomic and epidemiological evidence by an independent commission, not as a political judgement on any country's vaccine policy.
verbatim_quote: The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) informs that the review of the measles elimination status in the United States and Mexico will take place in November 2026, during the Commission's regular annual meeting of the Regional Verification Commission for the Elimination of Measles, Rubella, and Congenital Rubella Syndrome (RVC).
verbatim_list: For both the United States and Mexico, the analysis period for assessing the possible re-establishment of endemic measles transmission corresponds to one year from the onset of the reported outbreaks: 20 January 2025 in the United States and 1 February 2025 in Mexico.

topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
title: The White House Takes Another Shot at Changing U.S. Childhood Vaccine Recommendations
key_claim: The 10 August executive order directs separate rather than combination MMR shots, empowers an HHS task force of federal officials that could bypass ACIP, and directs the Attorney General to challenge conflicting state laws, but 30 states including DC have already decoupled from federal recommendations and courts have blocked the earlier revised schedule.
frame_summary: KFF argues the order is unlikely to move US vaccine policy because the federal lever has lost its grip on the states and the courts, and that its main effect will be confusion among parents rather than changed practice.
verbatim_quote: Given ongoing legal challenges to the administration's vaccine actions and declining influence of federal recommendations on states vaccine policy decisions, it is not clear how much the new EO can shift U.S. vaccine policy.
verbatim_list: In fact, most states - 30 including DC - have already made moves to decouple their vaccine policies from federal government recommendations for one or more childhood vaccines, instead relying on prior recommendations, state recommendations, and/or those of external entities such as American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP).

Any recommendations from the Task Force are also unlikely to change how insurance covers childhood vaccinations given that private insurers have pledged to maintain existing childhood vaccine coverage through the end of 2027

title: Latest Global Immunization Coverage Estimates Illustrate Gaps in Vaccine Access
date_evidence:
Published

July 27, 2026

Latest Global Immunization Coverage Estimates Illustrate Gaps in Vaccine Access
key_claim: WHO and UNICEF estimates show global immunisation coverage was broadly flat in 2025, with 13.5 million zero-dose children and measles first-dose coverage stalled at 84% against a 95% target.
frame_summary: IVAC argues that flat coverage combined with falling global health financing puts immunisation targets out of reach, and that zero-dose children in fragile settings need different strategies rather than more of the same.
verbatim_quote: An estimated 13.5 million zero-dose children did not receive their first dose of DTP vaccine in 2025, approximately 750,000 fewer children than 2024, but far too many children continue to miss out on life-saving vaccines.
verbatim_list: Measles vaccine coverage has also stalled, with only 84% of children receiving their first dose of measles-containing vaccine (MCV1) and just 77% receiving their second dose.

topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
title: Germany Plans More Cuts to Global Health Funding, But Policymakers Push Back on 2027 Draft Budget
key_claim: Germany's draft 2027 budget cuts the flexible operational fund for international public health by 15.3% to EUR 47.33 million while total federal spending rises 5.9% on defence, with Germany now the largest government contributor to WHO after the US withdrawal.
frame_summary: The piece argues Germany is subordinating global health to defence and national interest, and that the cuts fall precisely on the flexible funds that pay for outbreak response rather than on the headline pledges that attract attention.
verbatim_quote: This affects almost exclusively the central operational fund for strengthening international public health, which Berlin is planning to slash by 15.3% to €47.33 million.
verbatim_list: Since the US's withdrawal from WHO, the Federal Republic has become the largest government contributor.

While the overall draft budget for 2027 is set to expand by 5.9% to a total of €555.4 billion, driven by increased defence spending, Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil is enforcing strict fiscal discipline in other policy areas.
The Bundestag expects to finalise the budget in late autumn.

topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
publisher: Health Policy Watch (Pan American Health Organization)
title: US Proposal to Eliminate PAHO Funding Raises Alarm Over Health Security in Americas
key_claim: The US FY2027 budget request proposes eliminating funding to PAHO, which has already adopted a 17% budget reduction and expects to fall from 1,042 posts to about 869, while the US owes nearly $135 million in member fees since 2024.
frame_summary: The piece argues that removing US funding from the regional body that provides early warning would leave the United States less able to detect disease threats before they arrive, and reports bipartisan security officials making that case against the administration.
verbatim_quote: In response to unpaid US dues, PAHO, the WHO's regional arm with 35 member states across the Americas, has adopted a 17% reduction in its upcoming budget.
verbatim_list: Across the organization, total positions are projected to drop from 1,042 during the 2024-2025 budget cycle to approximately 869 positions across 2026-2027.
In 2025 alone, PAHO's regional surveillance system analyzed 2.1 million disease threat data points, detecting 157 public health events across the Americas, the organization said.

title: Namibia Rejects US Demands for Data and Pathogen-Sharing
key_claim: Namibia has rejected US demands for health data and pathogen sharing attached to a bilateral replacement for PEPFAR support worth around $45 million a year, joining Zimbabwe and Ghana, while the Kenya and DRC agreements face legal challenge.
frame_summary: The piece argues that US bilateral health agreements demanding pathogen access without guaranteed benefit-sharing are a direct challenge to the multilateral PABS system, and that recipient states are refusing the terms even at the cost of losing funding.
cluster: Access settled by bargain, not by rule
verbatim_quote: However, the US withdrew from the WHO when Donald Trump assumed the presidency in January 2025, and its bilateral health agreements, which demand access to pathogen information without guaranteeing that any benefits will be shared, are a direct challenge to a WHO PABS system.
verbatim_list: In the past few years, the country has received around $45 million a year in support from the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), and a total of over $1 billion since 2003.

Zimbabwe and Ghana have also rejected the US data- and pathogen-sharing demands, while the memorandums of understanding (MOUs) that the US has reached with Kenya and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) both face legal challenges from civil society groups.

topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
title: WHO Member States continue negotiations on the Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing Annex
date_evidence:
WHO Member States continue negotiations on the Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing Annex

20 July 2026

News release

Geneva
key_claim: The seventh IGWG meeting closed in July without a finalised PABS annex, leaving contractual arrangements, laboratory network structure and the definition of benefits unresolved, with the eighth meeting set for 14 to 18 September 2026.
frame_summary: WHO argues that a negotiated multilateral PABS system is the route to rapid pathogen sharing with fair benefit return, and presents the remaining disagreements as bridgeable rather than as evidence the multilateral route is failing.
cluster: Access settled by bargain, not by rule
verbatim_quote: WHO Member States have advanced negotiations on the Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing (PABS) annex, a central component of the WHO Pandemic Agreement, while agreeing that continued discussions are needed to finalize a framework that supports a faster, more effective and equitable response to future pandemics.
verbatim_list: The IGWG will hold its eighth meeting from 14-18 September 2026.

Discussions focused on several interrelated elements of the PABS system, including the contractual arrangements underpinning the framework, the structure of the laboratory networks responsible for the sharing and handling of pathogens with pandemic potential and their sequence information, and the definition of benefits arising from pathogen sharing.

topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
title: What to Know About the BALANCE Model for GLP-1s in Medicare and Medicaid and the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge
key_claim: CMS delayed the BALANCE Model indefinitely after Part D sponsor uptake fell short of an 80% participation threshold, extending the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge instead at a $245 net monthly price through the end of 2027.
frame_summary: KFF argues that GLP-1 access rests on fragile temporary demonstration authority rather than statutory entitlement, leaving beneficiaries facing a coverage cliff and payers unwilling to absorb unquantified cost risk.
verbatim_quote: Manufacturers have agreed to provide eligible GLP-1s under the Bridge program at a net price of $245 per month supply.

topic: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
title: How well are AI-discovered drugs faring in the clinic?
key_claim: Few AI-discovered drugs have reached late-stage trials, with Insilico's rentosertib now in a 52-week phase 3 in China and Recursion posting a polyp-burden reduction, set against failures such as Verge Genomics' ALS candidate.
frame_summary: The piece argues that AI's apparent early-phase advantage remains unproven where it matters, and that the technology's real test is whether a small number of closely watched assets survive mid-stage and late-stage efficacy trials.
verbatim_quote: Insilico also has its own candidates in the works as part of an expansive pipeline that includes over 40 programs in a wide swath of indications.
verbatim_list: Most patients in the trial continued to show reductions even after they were off the medication for 12 weeks - a promising sign for a condition with no existing treatment options.
